says: A Process object's swap RPC hands its request to the runner undecoded, so an empty program or hash reaches Schema make in the runner's refusal and the swap dies with a defect, while the restart RPC beside it decodes its request first.
proof: next/packages/libfabrika/src/cloudflare/runtime.ts:2644 `swap: (request: Parameters<typeof runner.swap>[0]) => attributed(runner.swap(request))` passes the request as typed, with no decode; :2653-2655 `restart: (request: unknown) => Schema.decodeUnknownEffect(RestartRequest)(request).pipe(Effect.mapError(... bad_row ...))` decodes. In the runner, an empty `program` fails `loader.load` or the name check and calls `refuse("load")`, which runs `RuntimeRecord.cases["code.refused"].make({ program: request.program, hash: request.hash, ... })` (next/packages/libfabrika/src/runtime/Runner.ts:2724-2725), whose `program` and `hash` are `Schema.NonEmptyString` (next/packages/libfabrika/src/runtime/ProcessStore.ts:66-71), so make throws.
cost: A malformed swap call from the wire answers a defect, not a typed error; today the only caller is the Project's own code push (runtime.ts:1718), so the cost is low until another caller exists.
